messages.subject: INLA spatio-temporal output
parts:
Dear INLA experts:

I recently used R-INLA for a space-time model, I have one question regarding the spatio-temporal estimates.

In the original data, I have some FIPS missing their covriates and outcome, the other FIPS have some of the covariates missing and these records are organized by year (8 years)

In the model, I have a spatially unstructured random effect, a spatially structured effect, and a space-time interaction (I used for "besag" space effect and "rw1" for time effect).

After the model fitting, I looked at my output and here is my question:

1. There are some FIPS with very big SD. , and these FIPS happened to be those missing their covriates and outcome, so the big SD is a result of the missing value ?
2. What "kld" means in the output ?


I attached the result. 


Thanks so much for spending your valuable time helping out !! I had a hard time in exploring the problems..



Xiao

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA spatio-temporal output
parts:
Covariates with missing values need to be modeled explicitly, or the associated data points not used.
Missing values in covariates are interpreted as "zero effect", which is probably not what you want.

But I'm not familiar with the acronym "FIPS", so perhaps I've misunderstood the problem.

Finn

parts:
Hi Dear Dr.Lindgren,

Thanks for the reply, "FIPS" is like zipcode, it's basically a kind of area index in U.S, sorry I didn't make it clear in the original post.

Yes, I didn't include any of these areas (FIPS) in the data, the data only include those FIPS with no missing values.Thus when viewing the spatially unstructured random effect on the map, only some of the areas are colored accordingly.
  
But for the "besag" model, since the graph file I used is for the entire region, therefore, all the FIPS are fitted and displayed.

Now, here is my problem, I also fitted a space-time effect in the model, with "besag" for spatial effect and "rw1" for temporal effect. When I looked at the output of
space-time effect, those FIPS originally missing have very big SD. 
Can you give me some clue why this happened ?

By the way, in order to make the program workable, I used control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.1) ( without it, the program crushed ) .


Thanks in advance!
Xiao

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA spatio-temporal output
parts:
Finn

On 6 Oct 2015, at 20:21, Xiao Li <lixiao...@gmail.com>

Thanks for the reply, "FIPS" is like zipcode, it's basically a kind of area index in U.S, sorry I didn't make it clear in the original post.

Yes, I didn't include any of these areas (FIPS) in the data, the data only include those FIPS with no missing values.Thus when viewing the spatially unstructured random effect on the map, only some of the areas are colored accordingly.
So the fixed effects estimates should be ok then.
But for the "besag" model, since the graph file I used is for the entire region, therefore, all the FIPS are fitted and displayed.
Yes, this is as it should be.

Now, here is my problem, I also fitted a space-time effect in the model, with "besag" for spatial effect and "rw1" for temporal effect. When I looked at the output of
space-time effect, those FIPS originally missing have very big SD. 
Can you give me some clue why this happened ?

The simplest explanation would be that the besag model isn't a good fit to your data, so that the predictions simply are as uncertain as your results indicate. They should however normally not be larger than the variance of the data itself, so you can check if that's the case or not.

Finn

By the way, in order to make the program workable, I used control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.1) ( without it, the program crushed ) .


Thanks in advance!
Xiao
